pride_data.title: Targeted quantification of XL peptides in Bik1 variants and different conditions
pride_data.projectDescription: Quantification of crosslinks in Bik1 variants and different conditions (phase separation, soluble, supernatant, pellet)
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Bik1 FL and Bik1 variants (50µg, ~1mg/ml) were subjected to a crosslinking reaction with 1 mM isotope labelled di-succimidylsuberate (DSS-d0 and DSS-d12; CreativeMolecules Inc.).  After 30 min of incubation at 37C and 700rpm agitation in thermomixer, samples were quenched with 50mM NH3HCO3 pH =8. Upon quenching, samples were dried, dissolved in 8 M Urea, reduced with 5 mM TCEP, and alkylated with 10 mM iodoacetamide. The proteolysis was performed overnight at 37 ⁰C in 1M urea using trypsin 1:50 E:S, and then quenched with 5% formic acid. The detailed protocol of the reaction has been previously described by Leitner et al. [Leitner, Nat Protocol 2014] LC-MS/MS measurements were performed on an Orbitrap QExactive+ mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher) coupled to Dionex Ultimate liquid chromatography system. Peptides were loaded on a commercial trap column and separated across a 45 min gradient: from 8% to 25% in 40 min and from 25% to 50% in 5 min (buffer A: 0.1% (v/v) formic acid; buffer B: 0.1% (v/v) formic acid, 95% (v/v) acetonitrile) using a reverse phase column (Thermo PepMap RSLCcolumn, 15 cm length, 75 μm inner diameter). The MS acquisition of targeted peptide (17 crosslinks heavy and light and 1 householder peptides for Bik1 peptides) was set up with the combination of one MS1 untargeted scan (R=70’000 at 400m/z, maxIT = 64ms, AGC= 3e6) and 37 scheduled targeted scan (R=70’000 at 400m/z, maxIT = auto, AGC= 1e5) using an isolation window of 1.4m/z and HCD fragmentation (NCE=28%) .
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: A library based on conformotypic peptides previous identified by xQuest was generated. Only common transitions from light and heavy crosslinked peptides were used for this analysis. The quantification of targeted peptides was manually performed using Skyline-daily based on the following criteria: (1) co-elution of heavy and light cross-linked peptides, (2) matching of the peak shape, and (3) matching intensity for at least five common transitions of heavy and light crosslinked peptides (transitions shared between the light and heavy form of the crosslinked peptide). For more info se [Mehnert et al Nat Commun 2020]. The abundance of crosslinked peptides was then calculated by summing the integrated area of ten common transitions per peptide (five transitions for the heavy and light forms of the crosslinked peptide, respectively). Crosslinked peptides were normalized for the intensity of two non-crosslinked Bik1 peptides (MVLEEVQPTFDR). The significance of change for the log2 abundance of the crosslinked peptides was estimated with p values using a two-sided, not paired t-test.
